coverage_notes: Exercises creation of a new Python module with wraparound arithmetic, negative inputs, and input immutability.
Exercises localized repair inside a class while preserving related methods and unrelated workspace files.

tests.description: Creates a sequence rotation helper that handles empty input, large and negative step counts, and does not mutate its argument.
tests.script:
import solution
request = {
    'task': 'Create sequences.py with a function rotate_left(values, steps). It must return a new list containing the values rotated left by steps positions. Steps must wrap for values larger than the sequence length, negative steps must rotate right, and an empty input must return an empty list. Do not mutate the supplied sequence.',
    'files': {'guide.txt': 'Sequence utilities\n'}
}
response = solution.handle_request(request)
assert isinstance(response, dict)
assert set(response) == {'files'}
files = response['files']
assert files['guide.txt'] == 'Sequence utilities\n'
assert isinstance(files.get('sequences.py'), str)
namespace = {}
exec(compile(files['sequences.py'], 'sequences.py', 'exec'), namespace)
rotate_left = namespace['rotate_left']
values = [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert rotate_left(values, 1) == [2, 3, 4, 1]
assert rotate_left(values, 6) == [3, 4, 1, 2]
assert rotate_left(values, -1) == [4, 1, 2, 3]
assert rotate_left([], 100) == []
assert values == [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert rotate_left(('a', 'b', 'c'), 3) == ['a', 'b', 'c']
print('rotation-ok')

tests.description: Repairs a defective class method while retaining constructor and reset behavior and preserving an unrelated document.
tests.script:
import solution
source = '''class Counter:\n    def __init__(self, start=0):\n        self.value = start\n\n    def increment(self, amount=1):\n        self.value -= amount\n        return self.value\n\n    def reset(self):\n        self.value = 0\n        return self.value\n'''
request = {
    'task': 'Fix Counter.increment in counter.py so it adds amount to the current value and returns the updated value. Preserve the constructor and reset behavior, and do not change unrelated files.',
    'files': {'counter.py': source, 'CHANGELOG.md': 'Initial release\n'}
}
response = solution.handle_request(request)
assert set(response) == {'files'}
files = response['files']
assert files['CHANGELOG.md'] == 'Initial release\n'
namespace = {}
exec(compile(files['counter.py'], 'counter.py', 'exec'), namespace)
Counter = namespace['Counter']
counter = Counter(10)
assert counter.value == 10
assert counter.increment() == 11
assert counter.increment(4) == 15
assert counter.increment(-3) == 12
assert counter.reset() == 0
assert counter.increment(2) == 2
print('counter-repair-ok')

tests.description: Adds a validated chunking function to an existing module without breaking its existing helper or unrelated data.
Processes multiple valid JSON requests in one CLI session, ignores an intervening blank line, and emits exactly one ordered JSON response per request.
tests.script:
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import solution
requests = [
    {'task': 'No changes are required. Return the complete workspace unchanged.', 'files': {'alpha.txt': 'A\n', 'src/a.py': 'VALUE = 1\n'}},
    {'task': 'Keep every file unchanged and return the workspace.', 'files': {'beta.txt': 'B\n'}}
]
stdin_text = json.dumps(requests[0]) + '\n\n' + json.dumps(requests[1]) + '\n'
completed = subprocess.run([sys.executable, solution.__file__], input=stdin_text, text=True, capture_output=True)
assert completed.returncode == 0, (completed.returncode, completed.stdout, completed.stderr)
lines = completed.stdout.splitlines()
assert len(lines) == 2, completed.stdout
responses = [json.loads(line) for line in lines]
assert responses == [{'files': requests[0]['files']}, {'files': requests[1]['files']}]
assert '```' not in completed.stdout
assert 'Traceback' not in completed.stdout
print('cli-batch-ok')
